cases.documentary_assessment: Opening: the two restored reference letters correspond by order to two printed lacuna dots. The final doubtful reference vowel corresponds to the later single lacuna dot, not its closing bracket. Printed letters between these ranges lack the reference underdots. This is a positional/qualification comparison; the editor rejects the final vowel reading and no restoration is adopted.
Final punctuation: the reference terminal colon has no corresponding printed colon in the revised line. Record a punctuation difference, without inventing a lost sign or deleting the reference colon.

Opening damaged group: the reference isolated dot corresponds to the printed doubtful consonant before chi. Chi has a different doubt status and the later letter forms differ. The anchored group identifies the compared position; neither disputed letter becomes a project reading.

Before eke: the reference curly-braced colon is not present in the printed revised sequence. Preserve the opaque reference intervention and absence of a matching printed colon; do not decode the braces as a new accepted correction.

After abura: reference angle-entity notation and its enclosed letter have no printed counterpart in this revised graphic layer. Record the editorial-layer difference, not a newly verified omitted ancient letter.

In the titbeti group: the source has a doubtful alternative consonant; its apparatus preference is qualified. The reference underdot does not make the competing letters equal or secure either reading.
Initial sign of qlaxa group: base correspondence holds under the recorded convention, but the printed underdot must be retained. The apparatus preference is not independent project certainty.
Within zpplide: the printed consonant has an underdot absent from the corresponding reference letter. Preserve this uncertainty difference.
In the following kãta group: the revised consonant differs from the reference vowel and the opaque exclamation mark is separate editorial notation. No spelling correction is applied.
In the final trqqnta group: the printed consonant is underdotted where the reference counterpart is not. Retain the source qualification; the apparatus discusses damage rather than project certainty.

Opening of source label3: within the existing provisional carryover allocation, the restored reference consonant corresponds to the printed underdotted consonant before the shared following letters. The source’s bracketed edge-occupancy question precedes that consonant and must not be paired with it as a letter. This does not certify the physical boundary.
After the initial damaged group: a reference colon has no printed counterpart at this position. Distinguish the literal source punctuation schemes without inferring lexical division.

In the damaged kibeda range: printed qualification differs and the lacuna has optional-position notation absent from the reference. The reference underdots, spaces and opaque bracket extent remain literal. Do not treat the optional parenthesis as an ancient sign.

In the following pabana range: the reference consonant corresponds to the single printed lacuna dot between shared flanking letters. Brackets are delimiters, not substitute consonants; the editor’s damaged-position discussion does not identify an accepted replacement.

Before the stanza divider after kuprime: the reference colon is absent in the revised print. The apparatus explicitly questions crowded points; this is punctuation comparison, not a certified deletion on the monument.

After the doubtful p: both layers have punctuation, but the reference curly marks and printed underlined colon express different editorial qualifications. Keep underlined punctuation separate from the doubt of the preceding letter.

At the qir/ze transition: curly intervention markers and different print spacing accompany a punctuation correspondence. The reference entities are kept opaque; this is not evidence for a lexical split.

In the slitami range: the printed letter differs from the reference letter/exclamation sequence. Retain the spelling intervention as an editorial-layer issue and the following doubtful consonant separately.

In the final kuprimesi continuation: the printed consonant differs from the reference nasal form, and the reference exclamation/angle intervention has no printed counterpart. This comparison of printed forms does not select a corrected ancient spelling.

In the final damaged group: two restored reference letters correspond in order to the two printed lacuna dots. The intervening print space is layout, not another sign. The shared outer letters anchor this range without validating either restoration.

At source label4 opening: the reference places a letter plus question mark inside its bracket, whereas the print brackets only the occupancy question. Record the extra proposed reference letter without accepting it.

At the following consonant: the source print does not carry the reference underdot. Preserve the difference; the apparatus’s expressed doubt remains separate prose evidence, so absence of a printed dot does not establish a certain ancient reading.

After apiti: the reference bracketed space/letter and the printed three-dot lacuna are comparable as ranges. The evidence does not identify which printed unknown position the restored letter occupies. Keep the range correspondence and prohibit a unique per-letter pairing.

At the lijanuwa opening: the print explicitly preserves the p/l alternative at one comparative position, while the reference has one doubtful form. Neither alternative is eliminated and the later reconstruction is not substituted.

Inside mruwasi: the doubtful reference consonant corresponds to the single printed lacuna dot, not the bracket closing it. Shared flanking letters identify the position; the lost sign’s identity remains open.

At sebe: the reference intervention and printed graphic consonant belong to different editorial layers. The apparatus identifies an emendation in the older edition; no copying error or accepted replacement is inferred.
After lajata: the printed separator has an underdot not present in the reference separator. Record the visible typographic mark; its exact editorial interpretation remains qualified.

At epedes: the same base letter is carried by different editorial context because the reference braces it. Preserve this context difference without assigning an undocumented meaning to the braces or treating the letter as newly attested.
At wes/nteli: a printed colon corresponds to reference punctuation enclosed by opaque curly marks. Print spacing is not an ancient lexical boundary.
Before the final t[u] group: the print has a colon without a reference punctuation partner. Retain this source punctuation difference; do not add it to the frozen row.

At the end of source label4: the print retains a bracketed unknown position. Keep this end-range uncertainty and the following digital carryover allocation distinct; it does not establish the exact physical end of the inscription line.

Opening of source label5: the two three-letter ranges differ under the provisional cross-row allocation, and the cost model admits shifted pairings. The printed text does not prove a unique correspondence for the first two digital letters. Record a range comparison, not an adopted character-by-character correction.
Within the opening damaged range: the printed bracket closes before punctuation whereas the reference bracket extent differs. A bracket delimiter is not an ancient lost sign.
Before erei: reference restoration and bracket extent differ from the revised print. Preserve the entire damaged range; do not convert the proposed reference consonant into an observed source sign.
Inside ereimedi: the restored reference consonant corresponds to a single printed lacuna dot between shared flanks. The restoration is compared positionally, not validated.
Before ijesi: the revised print brackets a colon absent from the reference string at this point. This is qualified editorial punctuation, not an additional independently verified sign.

In the following ala range: reference extra/doubtful material differs from the shorter printed group. The trailing reference vowel and printed colon must remain unpaired because a delimiter is not a competing letter. Other forms and doubts are retained without a monument-level correction.
After trqqiz: the printed colon is underlined. The corresponding unmarked reference colon is not equivalent in uncertainty; retain the distinction.

In the sebuwedriz range: the print has underlined punctuation where the reference uses curly intervention markers. Preserve both the mark and the opaque reference notation; do not silently harmonize the word division.

In the gods-group: printed consonant/vowel values and the reference editorial context differ. Punctuation before the following stanza divider is not the same in the two layers. No reconstructed form is adopted.

After tuwi: the reference curly punctuation has no corresponding printed colon. The print’s vacat notice is an editor’s spacing description, not an ancient letter or an automatically equivalent delimiter.
In the group following seberbbi: underdot states, nasal-mark encoding and the printed additional vowel differ. The two nasal combining characters are not silently normalized to one reading.
At the following verb opening: the same initial base occurs with reference curly intervention context absent from print. This is qualification/context difference, not newly admitted evidence.
At the neriu group: the reference angle intervention and enclosed letter differ from the printed vowel. Keep both source forms attributed and do not substitute the reconstruction.

Across muwaxa/tuwemedi: print and reference differ in bracket extent, punctuation and doubt state. Printed apparent preservation and older restoration are separate source assertions, not project autopsy.
After xaba: the printed colon is underlined and its apparatus describes punctuation as possible. Preserve that qualification rather than make the reference colon independently certain.

At source label6 end: the print includes an edge-occupancy question after the final letter. The reference has no corresponding bracketed question. Do not count the question as a restored ancient character.
At mlu: the revised underdot is absent from the corresponding reference vowel. Keep the letter-identification doubt even though the base agrees.
At the tuta group: the printed first consonant differs from the doubtful reference first consonant. The apparatus treats the older form as an emendation; no new canonical consonant is selected.
Following that group: the print contains punctuation absent from the frozen reference at the corresponding position. Record the punctuation scheme without imposing a lexical boundary.

At the luwadladi transition: reference angle intervention has no counterpart in the revised graphic string. The source wrap hyphen is print layout and cannot substitute for the reference proposed letter.

At the ubre/abrala junction: nasal-vowel state, uncertain reference letters and the printed delimiter/consonant pattern differ. The apparatus reports competing older observations. The anchors establish a range comparison, but the evidence does not establish unique pairings of the intervening digital letters to printed signs.

At source label7 end: print edge-occupancy notation is separate from the reference carryover ti. Retain the uncertain edge and do not turn the question into a new sign or a certified physical boundary.

At the aala group: the source nasal vowel differs from the reference first sign and its opaque exclamation/question/dot states. Retain both ranges and all uncertainties without a corrected project form.

Before the nasal final vowel in the sseps range: the print has a two-letter repeated run where the reference has one. The range-length difference is documentary; nothing establishes which of the identical printed letters would be the one-to-one partner. Keep a one-to-two run correspondence, not a uniquely identified omitted ancient sign.
At source label8 end: the reference angle-intervention letter is absent from the revised graphic text. The following print vacat is an editorial description, not that letter.

In source label9: curly reference punctuation and spacing differ from print. Keep the source-specific uncertainty on the following letter; the same printed separator is not implicitly present in the reference.

At the final damaged range: reference dots, source doubtful-letter typography and the printed stanza divider do not supply unique point pairings. The apparatus discusses a heavily damaged sign and a clear divider; the font-decoded terminal letter identity remains a printed-typography observation, not a new accepted reading. Keep the whole range and its qualification, including the final reference dots.
